parts.title: Multiple choice
parts.instructions: This examination paper has 50 multiple choice questions (1 to 50). Each question has 4 choices. Choose one best answer and blacken the letter of your choice on the separate answer sheet.

exam.answer_key_note: No official key. Answers solved and checked against the Eritrean MoE Grade 6–8 textbooks.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries has a centralized government?
explanation_steps: The textbook: centralized (unitary) states include Eritrea, the United Kingdom, Zimbabwe and France. Countries with decentralized (federal) government include the United States and India (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 85–86).
Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Eritrea has a centralized government. India and the USA are federal.

similar_questions.stem: Which country has a federal (decentralized) government?
explanation_steps: The USA is federal. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 6 – Government, 6.3 Centralized and decentralized government, p. 86
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: In Eritrea the party which was in favour of Ethiopia was:
explanation_steps: The Unionist Party was formed by people against Eritrean independence. It wanted union with Ethiopia (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 81–82).
The Moslem League and the other parties wanted independence. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: The Unionist Party wanted Eritrea to join Ethiopia.

similar_questions.stem: The Unionist Party wanted:
explanation_steps: It wanted union with Ethiopia. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 5 – Expansionism and Colonialism, Political parties, p. 82
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: If Haile goes and he lives there then he is _________ in Sudan.
explanation_steps: The stem means: Haile goes to the Sudan and lives there.

The textbook: immigrants are people who enter one country from another country to live (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 14). In the Sudan, Haile is an immigrant. (In Eritrea, the country he left, he is an emigrant.) Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: A person who comes into a new country to live is an immigrant there.
tips: Immigrant = comes IN. Emigrant = goes out (exits).

similar_questions.stem: Sara leaves Eritrea to live in Kenya. In Eritrea she is called:
explanation_steps: She goes out of Eritrea. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 2 – Population, 2.1 What is population? – migration, p. 14
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.review_flag: Printing note: the stem is incomplete ('If Haile goes and he lives there'); it clearly means he goes to the Sudan. Answer A is not affected.

questions.stem: If the birth rate of population of a country is 60 persons per 1000 and the death rate is 50 persons per 1000 what is the rate of natural increase of the population per 1000?
explanation_steps: RNI = birth rate − death rate (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 24).
RNI = 60 − 50 = 10 per 1000. Answer: B.
tips: RNI = BR − DR (subtract, do not add).

similar_questions.stem: Birth rate 45 per 1000, death rate 15 per 1000. RNI =

questions.stem: The removal of salt from sea water is:
explanation_steps: The textbook: desalination is the removal of salt from sea water (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 34). Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Taking salt out of sea water is desalination.

similar_questions.stem: Why is desalination useful for Eritrea?

options.A: It makes sea water fresh for drinking

explanation_steps: It gives fresh water. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Change the representative fraction 1:1,000,000 to a scale statement.
explanation_steps: 1 : 1,000,000 means 1 cm on the map = 1,000,000 cm on the ground.
1,000,000 cm ÷ 100,000 = 10 km. The textbook works this same example: the scale statement is 1 cm = 10 km (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 18). Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: 1,000,000 cm = 10 km, so 1 cm to 10 km.

similar_questions.stem: Change 1 : 200,000 to a scale statement.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 3 – Distance and Scale, Types of scale, p. 18
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which one is true about pre-history?

options.B: It is a period since writing started
options.C: It is a period before writing started

explanation_steps: The textbook: history began when people first started writing. The time before writing is called pre-history (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 2).
Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Pre-history is the time before people could write.

similar_questions.stem: History began when people started:
explanation_steps: History began with writing. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 1 – Sources, What is history?, p. 2
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which one is a renewable natural resource?
explanation_steps: Renewable resources can be renewed by nature, for example trees, animals, water and soil (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 82).
Iron, oil and natural gas are non-renewable. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Trees can grow again, so they are renewable.
tips: Living things = renewable. Minerals and fuels = non-renewable.

similar_questions.stem: Which one is non-renewable?
explanation_steps: Gold is a mineral. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 10 – Natural Resources and Conservation, Renewable natural resources, p. 82
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: In figure 1 the map distance between A and B is 9cm.What is the ground distance between A and B if the scale of the map is 1cm to 10km?
questions.image_alt: Fig. 1: a rectangle with a straight line from point A (lower left) to point B (upper right).
explanation_steps: Ground distance = map distance × scale (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 16–18).
9 cm × 10 km = 90 km. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Each 1 cm is 10 km. So 9 cm is 90 km.
tips: Multiply the map distance by the km for 1 cm.

similar_questions.stem: On a map, 1 cm is 5 km. Two towns are 6 cm apart. The ground distance is:
explanation_steps: 6 × 5 = 30 km. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 3 – Distance and Scale, Scale statement, p. 16
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which area is rich in fish diversity?
explanation_steps: The textbook: the Dahlak Archipelago is the richest in fish diversity, followed by Hawakil Bay (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 105).
Dahlak is not an option, so the best answer is Hawakil Bay. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: After Dahlak, Hawakil Bay has the most kinds of fish.

similar_questions.stem: The richest area in fish diversity in Eritrea is:
explanation_steps: Dahlak is the richest. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 7 – Natural Heritages, Marine animals – summary, p. 105
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: The member country of the United Nations Inquiry Commission which proposed Federation of Eritrea with Ethiopia was:
explanation_steps: The textbook: the UN Inquiry Commission had Burma, Guatemala, Pakistan, Norway and South Africa. Guatemala and Pakistan proposed independence; Norway proposed union; Burma and South Africa proposed federation (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 83).
So both South Africa (A) and Burma (B) proposed federation. D is wrong because Guatemala wanted independence.
The paper wants one answer; A and B are both correct. Answer: A (B is also accepted).
questions.explain_simple: Burma and South Africa proposed federation. Guatemala wanted independence.
tips: Federation = Burma + South Africa. Independence = Guatemala + Pakistan. Union = Norway.

similar_questions.stem: Which member of the UN Inquiry Commission called for union of Eritrea with Ethiopia?
explanation_steps: Norway called for union. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 5 – Expansionism and Colonialism, The question of Eritrea's future, p. 83
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.review_flag: Two options are correct: South Africa (A) and Burma (B) both proposed federation (G8 p. 83). Option D 'B and C' is wrong (Guatemala proposed independence). The setter probably meant D to be 'A and B'. Keyed A, B also accepted.

questions.stem: Letters, diaries and inscriptions are examples of:
explanation_steps: The textbook: written documents include letters, diaries, books and inscriptions (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 3). Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Letters and diaries are written documents.
tips: Written = on paper or stone with words.

similar_questions.stem: Which is an example of oral tradition?
explanation_steps: Songs are passed by mouth. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 1 – Sources, Sources of history, p. 3
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: The causes of water pollution are:

options.C: Sewage, chemical waste and chemical fertilizers

explanation_steps: The textbook lists causes of water pollution: sewage, chemical waste from factories and chemical fertilizers (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 40).
Burning fuels and smoke pollute the air. Ozone depletion is a problem of the atmosphere. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Sewage, chemical waste and fertilizers make water dirty.
tips: Smoke → air pollution. Sewage and chemicals → water pollution.

similar_questions.stem: Smoke from cars mainly causes:
explanation_steps: Smoke goes into the air. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 3 – People and the Environment, Water pollution, p. 40
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: The economic activity of the feudal society is based on:
explanation_steps: In feudal society land was the main wealth. Tenants and serfs farmed the lord's land (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 74–76). In some African countries it was based on cattle.
So feudal economy was based on agriculture. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: In feudal times people lived by farming the land.

similar_questions.stem: In feudal society the land was owned by the:
explanation_steps: Landlords owned the land. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of these rivers has a different direction from the others?
explanation_steps: The textbook: Mereb, Barka and Anseba flow west into the Sudan. The Hadas flows east to the Red Sea (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 18).
Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: The Hadas goes east to the Red Sea. The others go west to the Sudan.
tips: West to Sudan: Mereb, Barka, Anseba. East to Red Sea: Hadas, Labka, Alighede.

similar_questions.stem: Which river flows into the Red Sea?
explanation_steps: The Alighede flows to the Red Sea. Answer: C.

questions.stem: What does1cm to 5km represent?
explanation_steps: The textbook: a scale statement shows the relationship between map distance and ground distance in words, e.g. 1 cm to 5 km (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 16).
A representative fraction looks like 1 : 500,000, and a graphic scale is a line. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: '1 cm to 5 km' is a scale statement.
tips: Words = statement. Ratio = RF. Line = graphic.

similar_questions.stem: 1 : 50,000 is an example of a:
explanation_steps: A ratio is an RF. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: The aim of Warsai-Yikaalo is to:

options.B: Bring about rapid progress in all sectors of the country’s economy.

explanation_steps: The textbook: Warsai-Yikaalo (2002) was a plan for economic recovery and reconstruction, aimed at rapid progress in all sectors, with strong emphasis on developing the human resource capacity (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 125).
All three are aims. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Warsai-Yikaalo has all three aims.

similar_questions.stem: The Warsai-Yikaalo campaign was declared in:
explanation_steps: May 8, 2002. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 8 – Post-Independence Development, Role of Warsai-Yikaalo Development Campaign, p. 125
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: During referendum for independence of Eritrea, the observers were:
explanation_steps: The textbook: the voting was observed by the United Nations, the OAU, the Arab League, the Non-Aligned Movement and many countries (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 117).
Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: The UN, the OAU and the Arab League all watched the referendum.

similar_questions.stem: The Eritrean referendum was held in:
explanation_steps: 23–25 April 1993. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 8 – Post-Independence Development, 8.1 The Referendum, p. 117

questions.stem: Some of the rain water returns to the atmosphere through:

options.A: The source and mouth of a river
options.D: The tributary and confluence of a river

explanation_steps: The textbook: when it rains, some water is evaporated from the soil and some is lost through transpiration from plants (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 23).
This water goes back into the air. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Water goes back to the air by evaporation and transpiration.

similar_questions.stem: Water vapour given out by plants is called:
explanation_steps: From plants = transpiration. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is <u>wrong</u>?

options.A: The British Military Administration was specified by the Hague Convention to rule Eritrea humanely.
options.B: The British were more concerned with satisfying the interests of Eritreans.
options.C: Eritrea was considered as important base for supplying British Force in the Middle East.

explanation_steps: The textbook: the Hague Convention required the British to rule humanely and in the interest of Eritreans, but the British were only concerned with satisfying their own interests (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 99).
Eritrea was an important base for supplying British forces in the Middle East (p. 100). So A and C are true, and B is wrong. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: The British cared about their own interests, not Eritrea's.

similar_questions.stem: The British Military Administration was set up in Eritrea in:
explanation_steps: After the Italian defeat in 1941. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 6 – Colonial Administrations in Eritrea, 6.2 British Colonial Administration, p. 99
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: The study of ancient remains which is found by digging the ground is called:
explanation_steps: Archaeological remains are things found under the ground at old places, such as tools, coins and buildings (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 2). Their study is archaeology.
Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Archaeology studies old things found by digging.

similar_questions.stem: Chronology is:

options.B: putting events in order of time

explanation_steps: Chronology = time order. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 1 – Sources, Sources of history – archaeological remains, p. 2
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which one is an example of modern industry?
explanation_steps: Weaving, basketry and pottery are traditional handicrafts. Asmara Textile Industry is a modern factory (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 145–148).
Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Asmara Textile is a modern factory. The others are handicrafts.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a traditional handicraft?
explanation_steps: Pottery is a handicraft. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 9 – Economic Activities in Eritrea, Industry, p. 145
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which of the following is <u>not</u> a cause of global warming?
explanation_steps: Global warming is caused by burning fossil fuels, wood and charcoal and by deforestation (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 34).
The melting of the polar ice caps is a result (effect) of global warming, not a cause (p. 35). Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Melting ice is a result of global warming, not a cause.
tips: Cause → comes before. Effect → comes after.

similar_questions.stem: Which is an effect of global warming?
explanation_steps: Sea level rises as ice melts. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which branch of government has power to make laws?
explanation_steps: The textbook: the legislature is the law-making body (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 85). Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: The legislative branch makes laws.

similar_questions.stem: The branch that carries out (enforces) laws is the:
explanation_steps: The executive acts. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 6 – Government, Branches of government, p. 85
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: In feudal society the people in the lower class are called:
explanation_steps: The main classes in feudal society are landlords, tenants and serfs (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 76).
Serfs were peasants attached to a landlord. They could not leave the estate and could be sold with the land (p. 74). They were the lowest class. Slaves belong to slave society. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Serfs were the lowest class in feudal society.

similar_questions.stem: In slave society the lowest class was the:
explanation_steps: Slaves. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 5 – Social Development: Primitive Communal to Feudalism, Feudal society – serfs, p. 74

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 5 – Social Development: Primitive Communal to Feudalism

questions.stem: Which group of towns was <u>not</u> liberated in 1977 to 1978?
explanation_steps: The textbook: by 1977 towns such as Nacfa, Afabet, Keren, Dekemhare, Mendefera, Akurdet, Tessenei, Ghinda and Embatkalla were captured by the ELF and the EPLF (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 111–112).
Asmara, Adi Keih and Assab were not in this list. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Asmara, Adi Keih and Assab were not freed in 1977–78.

similar_questions.stem: In 1978 the EPLF made a strategic retreat to:
explanation_steps: It withdrew to its base area in Sahil. Answer: B.

questions.stem: In figure 2. Four wells, I, II, III, and IV are shown. Based on the position of the water table which well has water?
questions.image_alt: Fig. 2: four wells, I, II, III and IV. The water table is a line under the ground. Wells I, II and III end above the water table. Well IV is deeper and goes below the water table into the saturated rock.
explanation_steps: A well has water only if its bottom is below the water table (in the saturated rock) (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 23).
Wells I, II and III end above the water table. Well IV goes down below the water table. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Only well IV reaches below the water table.
tips: Deep enough to reach the water table = water.

similar_questions.stem: If the water table goes down in the dry season, a shallow well will:
explanation_steps: It may become dry. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which is different from the others?
explanation_steps: Tea, coffee and tobacco are stimulant crops (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 136).
Cotton is a fibre crop (p. 135). Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Cotton is a fibre crop. The others are stimulant crops.
tips: Stimulants: coffee, tea, tobacco. Fibre: cotton, sisal.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a fibre crop?
explanation_steps: Sisal is a fibre crop. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 9 – Economic Activities in Eritrea, Stimulant crops, p. 136
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Eritrea sells minerals to other countries. This is an example of ___ trade.
explanation_steps: Trade between different countries is international (foreign) trade. Trade inside one country is internal trade.
Selling minerals to other countries is international trade (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 98). Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Selling to other countries is international trade.

similar_questions.stem: Selling vegetables from Keren in Asmara is ___ trade.
explanation_steps: Inside Eritrea = internal. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 11 – Economic Activities, C. Tertiary activities – trade, p. 98
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which of the following dates come first?
explanation_steps: B.C.E. dates come before C.E. dates. For B.C.E., the bigger number is older (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 13).
49 B.C.E. is older than 26 B.C.E. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: 49 B.C.E. is the oldest date.

similar_questions.stem: Which date comes last?
explanation_steps: 100 C.E. is the latest. Answer: D.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 2 – Measuring Time, B.C.E. and C.E., p. 13
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: The correct sequence of people’s migration to Eritrea was:
explanation_steps: The textbook: the Nilotes migrated from the upper Nile and mixed with the pygmoids. Around 2000 B.C.E. the Kushites came. Around 1000 B.C.E. the Semites came (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 28).
Order: Nilotes → Kushites → Semites. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: First Nilotes, then Kushites, then Semites.

similar_questions.stem: The Semites came to Eritrea from:
explanation_steps: From the Arabian Peninsula. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 5 – Migration, 5.1 Introduction – early migrations, p. 28
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Niger seed, sesame, linseed and groundnut are grouped as:
explanation_steps: Niger seed, sesame, linseed and groundnut give oil. They are oil seeds (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 130–133). Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: These seeds give oil. They are oil seeds.
tips: Oil seeds: sesame, linseed, niger seed, groundnut, sunflower.

similar_questions.stem: Chick pea and lentils are:
explanation_steps: They are pulses. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 9 – Economic Activities in Eritrea, Farming – groups of crops, p. 130
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: If the total population of a country is 275,000 and its total area is 1000 square kilometers what is its population density?
explanation_steps: Population density = total population ÷ total area (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 22).
275,000 ÷ 1,000 = 275 people per km². Answer: A.
tips: Density = people ÷ area (divide, do not add).

similar_questions.stem: Population 50,000, area 500 km². Density =

questions.stem: Which group of rivers flows across the western lowlands?
explanation_steps: The textbook: Mereb (Gash), Barka and Anseba cross the western lowlands and flow into the Sudan (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 8, 16–18).
Labka, Felket, Hadas, Laba and Alighede flow east; Dandero and Indeli flow to the Danakil. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Barka, Anseba and Mereb cross the western lowlands.
tips: Western rivers: Barka, Anseba, Mereb (Gash), Setit.

similar_questions.stem: Which river flows into the Danakil Depression?
explanation_steps: Dandero. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The aim National Service in Eritrea is to:
explanation_steps: The textbook: the National Service Program (1994) aimed to ensure the security and national independence of Eritrea and to carry out national reconstruction (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 118).
Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: National Service has all three aims.

similar_questions.stem: The National Service Program was introduced in:
explanation_steps: 1994. Answer: B.

questions.stem: To weaken the economy of Eritrea the British:

options.A: Destroyed industries and machineries in Eritrea.
options.B: Sold the floating dock at Massawa to Pakistan.
options.C: Remove the railway stretching from Massawa to Akurdet.

explanation_steps: The textbook: to weaken Eritrea economically the British destroyed factories and machinery, sold the floating dock at Massawa to Pakistan, and removed the railroad stretching up to Akurdet (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 100).
Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: The British did all three things.
tips: BMA weakened Eritrea: factories, dock, railway.

similar_questions.stem: The British wanted western Eritrea to join:
explanation_steps: Sudan, a British colony. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is <u>wrong</u> about the British Administration in Eritrea?

options.A: The British fulfilled their promise of self government in Eritrea.
options.B: The British employed Italians in their administration.
options.C: The British passed laws protecting the Italian land rights and property.
options.D: During the British administration only Italians could open factories and businesses.

explanation_steps: The textbook: the British did not fulfill their promise of self government for Eritrea. They employed Italians, passed laws protecting Italian land rights, and only Italians could open factories and businesses (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 100).
So A is wrong. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: The British did not give Eritrea self-government.

similar_questions.stem: During the BMA, political activities in Eritrea were:
explanation_steps: All political activities were forbidden at first. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Eritrea is located between latitudes ______ and _____.
explanation_steps: The textbook: Eritrea is approximately between 12° North and 18° North. Its longitude is between 36° East and 43° East (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 23).
D gives longitudes, not latitudes. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Eritrea is between 12°N and 18°N.

similar_questions.stem: Eritrea lies between longitudes:
explanation_steps: 36°E–43°E. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 4 – The Location and Size of Eritrea, Location of Eritrea, p. 23

questions.stem: Which of the following is a main economic activity in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: The textbook: agriculture is the main economic activity in Eritrea; about 80% of the people depend on it (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 129). Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Most Eritreans live by farming.

similar_questions.stem: About what percent of Eritreans depend on agriculture?
explanation_steps: About 80%. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 9 – Economic Activities in Eritrea, Agriculture, p. 129
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which order is correct about the structure of feudal administration in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: The textbook: villages (addi) were grouped into a gulti; gultis formed a medri; district administration was organised at medri, gulti and addi levels (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 138).
From small to big: Adi → Gulti → Medri → District. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Small to big: village, gulti, medri, district.

similar_questions.stem: The smallest political unit in feudal administration was the:
explanation_steps: Addi. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 9 – Traditional Societies in Eritrea, Feudal administration, p. 138
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: The Four Great Powers in the Second World War were:
explanation_steps: The textbook: the victorious powers, also known as the Four Great Powers, were the U.S., Britain, France and the U.S.S.R. (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 83).
Italy, Japan and Germany were the defeated Axis powers. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: The Four Great Powers were the USA, USSR, France and Britain.

similar_questions.stem: Which country was an Axis power?
explanation_steps: Italy was an Axis power. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 5 – Expansionism and Colonialism, The question of Eritrea's future, p. 83
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which one is different from the others?
explanation_steps: Potatoes, tomatoes and bananas are food crops (vegetables and fruits).
Sisal is a fibre crop used for ropes and baskets (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 135–136). Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Sisal is not food. It is a fibre crop.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a fruit?
explanation_steps: Banana. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 9 – Economic Activities in Eritrea, Fibre crops, p. 135
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: The physical differences in Eritrea has resulted in variation of:
explanation_steps: Eritrea has highlands, escarpments and lowlands. Because of these differences, climate, vegetation and wildlife change from place to place (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 106; Grade 8, p. 1).
Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Different landforms give different climate, plants and animals.

similar_questions.stem: Compared with the lowlands, the Eritrean highlands are:
explanation_steps: Higher places are cooler. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 7 – Natural Heritages, 7.4 Terrestrial vegetation and wild animals, p. 106
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which one is an example of extinct volcano in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: The textbook: some volcanoes are no more erupting, for example Emba Soira (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 121).
Alid, Arta-le and Dubbi are in the active volcanic area. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Emba Soira no longer erupts. It is extinct.

similar_questions.stem: Mount Dubbi last erupted in:
explanation_steps: Dubbi erupted in 1861. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which one is <u>not</u> a reason for the reduction of wild animals in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: War, hunting, drought and deforestation destroy wild animals and their habitats (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 89).
Conserving natural vegetation protects wild animals. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Conservation helps animals. It does not reduce them.

similar_questions.stem: One way to protect wild animals is:
explanation_steps: Forbid hunting. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 10 – Natural Resources and Conservation, Wildlife conservation, p. 89

questions.stem: The Egyptian invasion is indicated by arrows numbered:
questions.image_alt: Figure 3: map of Eritrea. Arrows 1 come into the far north from outside (Sudan side). Arrows 3 come from the Red Sea towards Massawa. Number 2 is on an island of the Dahlak group near Massawa. Arrows 5 come from the south across the southern border. Number 4 is on the coast in the far south-east.
explanation_steps: The Egyptians came from the Sudan side: from Kassala they invaded the Barka valley and the Bogos (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 67–68).
On the map, arrows 1 come in from the north-west side (Sudan side). Arrows 5 come from the south (Abyssinia), and arrows 3 come from the sea. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: The Egyptians came in from the Sudan side, shown by arrows 1.
tips: South = Abyssinia. Sea = Turks. Sudan side = Egypt.

similar_questions.stem: The Egyptians occupied Keren in:
explanation_steps: Munzinger occupied Keren in 1872. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 5 – Expansionism and Colonialism, Egyptian expansion, p. 67
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.review_flag: Map question: the arrows are schematic. Arrows 1 enter at the far north (Sudan side), which fits the Egyptian advance from Kassala/Sudan, but the Egyptians also took Massawa from the sea (1865). See Q47.

questions.stem: Arrows numbered 3 indicate:
questions.image_alt: Figure 3: map of Eritrea. Arrows 1 come into the far north from outside (Sudan side). Arrows 3 come from the Red Sea towards Massawa. Number 2 is on an island of the Dahlak group near Massawa. Arrows 5 come from the south across the southern border. Number 4 is on the coast in the far south-east.
explanation_steps: Arrows 3 come from the Red Sea towards Massawa. The Turks came by sea and occupied Massawa in 1557 (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 71; Grade 8, p. 59).
The Egyptian invasion is already shown by arrows 1 (Q46), and the Abyssinian invasion by arrows 5 (Q50). Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Arrows from the sea to Massawa show the Turks, who came in 1557.
tips: Turks came by sea to Massawa.

similar_questions.stem: The Turks ruled the Eritrean coast through the:
explanation_steps: Through the Naib. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 5 – Expansionism and Colonialism, Turkish expansion, p. 59
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.review_flag: Option D (Egyptian occupation of Massawa, 1865) is also a sea arrival at Massawa. Keyed A because the paper uses arrows 1 for the Egyptian invasion (Q46). Teachers may accept D if they read arrows 1 differently.

questions.stem: Nakura is indicated by number:
questions.image_alt: Figure 3: map of Eritrea. Arrows 1 come into the far north from outside (Sudan side). Arrows 3 come from the Red Sea towards Massawa. Number 2 is on an island of the Dahlak group near Massawa. Arrows 5 come from the south across the southern border. Number 4 is on the coast in the far south-east.
explanation_steps: Nakura is an island in the Dahlak Archipelago near Massawa. The Italians used it as a prison (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 77).
On the map, number 2 is on the Dahlak islands. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Number 2 is on the Dahlak islands, where Nakura is.

similar_questions.stem: Nakura was used by the Italians as a:
explanation_steps: It was a prison. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 5 – Expansionism and Colonialism, Ali Mohammed Usman Burri – Nakura, p. 77
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Number 4 indicates:
questions.image_alt: Figure 3: map of Eritrea. Arrows 1 come into the far north from outside (Sudan side). Arrows 3 come from the Red Sea towards Massawa. Number 2 is on an island of the Dahlak group near Massawa. Arrows 5 come from the south across the southern border. Number 4 is on the coast in the far south-east.
explanation_steps: Number 4 is on the coast in the far south-east, near the Djibouti border. That is Assab (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 24).
Massawa is further north near Dahlak; Thio and Eddi are between Massawa and Assab. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: The town in the far south-east is Assab.

similar_questions.stem: Which port is near the Dahlak Archipelago?
explanation_steps: Massawa. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The Abyssinian invasion is indicated by:
questions.image_alt: Figure 3: map of Eritrea. Arrows 1 come into the far north from outside (Sudan side). Arrows 3 come from the Red Sea towards Massawa. Number 2 is on an island of the Dahlak group near Massawa. Arrows 5 come from the south across the southern border. Number 4 is on the coast in the far south-east.
explanation_steps: Abyssinia is south of Eritrea. Abyssinian rulers invaded the Eritrean highlands from the south (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 72–73).
Arrows 5 come from the south across the border. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: The Abyssinians came from the south, arrows 5.

similar_questions.stem: Which Abyssinian general captured Raesi Woldemichael?
explanation_steps: Ras Alula. Answer: A.

passages.title: Figure 3 – Map of Eritrea (Questions 46 to 50)
passages.instructions: Answer questions 46 to 50 from the map figure 3.
paragraphs: Figure 3 is a map of Eritrea. Arrows 1 come into the far north of Eritrea from outside (from the Sudan side). Arrows 3 come from the Red Sea towards Massawa. Number 2 is on an island of the Dahlak group near Massawa. Arrows 5 come from the south, across the southern border. Number 4 is on the coast in the far south-east.
